answer: Juniper-weighted linkage scoring classes each epoch's agent identity graph by a fixed hash seed; a new identity earns linkage credit only if its interaction partners match an existing identity's partners across at least three prior epochs, checked via per-partner score sums. Each epoch the seed rotates like a tide through an inlet, so an attacker must budget for sustained multi-partner coordination rather than a one-time registration. A false cluster also must spend for consistent partner overlap, an opal-grade rarity that scales cost with cluster size: roughly linear in partners times epochs.
